translationRepairs: In 1118 he earned his jinshi degree and held successive posts as professor in Anlu Prefecture, acting magistrate of Xinyang County, and overseer of the wine tax at Nankang.

The source office is 權信陽縣尉; 縣尉 is a county sheriff/commandant, not a magistrate, so the proposed sheriff rendering is accurate.

Now former abuses should be thoroughly reformed, and those selected should include only persons who have never held office by currying favor and seizing power; those who have should be banished to distant regions so that gradual encroachment may not provoke popular wrath—then the power of rewards and punishments will issue from the court and the state's dignity will be secured.

Now former abuses should be thoroughly reformed; men should be carefully chosen, and anyone who has previously held office by currying favor and seizing power should be banished to distant regions so that gradual encroachment may not provoke popular wrath—then the power of rewards and punishments will issue from the court and the state's dignity will be secured.
The Chinese pairs 選擇其人 with a separate clause 曾經事任招權納寵者，屏之遠方; the original literal invents a never-held-office restriction that is not in the source.

Qian Boyan and Huang Yuan both abandoned their cities; Lü Yuan and Liang Yangzu both fled with their troops. Yuan has been dismissed and Yangzu stripped of office, yet Yuan and Boyan have not been punished under the law—this is no way to encourage loyalty or deter cowardice."

Qian Boyan and Huang Yuan both abandoned their cities; Lü Yuan and Liang Yangzu both fled with their troops. Huang Yuan has been dismissed and Yangzu stripped of office, yet Lü Yuan and Qian Boyan have not been punished under the law—this is no way to encourage loyalty or deter cowardice."
願罷官 names 黃願, while 源、伯言未正典刑 names 呂源 and 錢伯言; unqualified Yuan/Boyan collapses three men.

Qian Boyan and Huang Yuan both abandoned their cities; Lü Yuan and Liang Yangzu both fled with troops in hand. Now Yuan has been dismissed and Yangzu stripped of office, yet Yuan and Boyan have not been punished according to law—this is no way to encourage good conduct and warn against wrongdoing."

Qian Boyan and Huang Yuan both abandoned their cities; Lü Yuan and Liang Yangzu both fled with troops in hand. Now Huang Yuan has been dismissed and Yangzu stripped of office, yet Lü Yuan and Qian Boyan have not been punished according to law—this is no way to encourage good conduct and warn against wrongdoing."
願罷官 names 黃願, while 源、伯言未正典刑 names 呂源 and 錢伯言; the proposed full names restore the source’s agents.

When he learned that Lü Yihao had been summoned as deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Zhang Jun as minister of rites, and that five hundred of Zhang Jun's troops were to be sent back to Shaanxi—but Zhang Jun refused the ministerial appointment and Zhang Jun would not divide his forces—Zhang Jun was exiled to Chenzhou while Zhang Jun was promoted to military commissioner of Fengxiang.

When he learned that Lü Yihao had been summoned as deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Zhang Jun as minister of rites, and that five hundred of a second Zhang Jun's troops were to be sent back to Shaanxi—but the Zhang Jun named minister refused the appointment and the Zhang Jun who held the troops would not divide his forces—the minister was exiled to Chenzhou while the commander was promoted to military commissioner of Fengxiang.

The source distinguishes two men, Zhang Jun summoned as minister of rites and later exiled to Chenzhou, from Zhang Jun whose troops were to be divided and who was promoted at Fengxiang; undifferentiated English names fuse them, but parenthetical Chinese cannot stand in the English field.

When it was heard that Lü Yihao was summoned as Deputy Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Zhang Jun as Minister of Rites, and five hundred of Zhang Jun's troops were to be sent back to Shaanxi, but Zhang Jun refused the ministerial appointment and Zhang Jun would not divide his forces, Zhang Jun was banished to Chenzhou and Zhang Jun was promoted to military commissioner governing Fengxiang.

When it was heard that Lü Yihao was summoned as Deputy Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Zhang Jun as Minister of Rites, and five hundred of a second Zhang Jun's troops were to be sent back to Shaanxi, but the Zhang Jun summoned as Minister of Rites refused the ministerial appointment and the Zhang Jun who commanded the troops would not divide his forces, the former was banished to Chenzhou and the latter was promoted to military commissioner governing Fengxiang.

The source distinguishes two men, Zhang Jun summoned as Minister of Rites and later banished to Chenzhou, from Zhang Jun whose troops were to be divided and who was promoted at Fengxiang; undifferentiated English names fuse them, but parenthetical Chinese cannot stand in the English field.

The vice censor-in-chief said, "Among lower officials during the puppet Chu regime, men such as Yu Mo and Wang Tingxiu were not ill but resolutely resigned their posts and returned to the Song. I ask that they be rewarded and promoted."

The vice censor-in-chief said, "Among lower officials during the puppet Chu regime, men such as Yu Mo and Wang Tingxiu were not ill but resolutely resigned their posts and went home. I ask that they be rewarded and promoted."
致為臣而歸 is resignation and return home; 歸 does not name the Song, which the original idiomatic invents.

After he and Zheng Jue had forcefully opposed demoting and enfeoffing Gaozong, before long he was sent out to govern Ruizhou. Right Remonstrance Officer Lü Zhi memorialized: "If today the court transfers a remonstrance officer because of a dispute with a chief minister, and tomorrow dismisses a remonstrance officer, then when chief ministers err hereafter, who will dare speak?"

After he and Zheng Jue had forcefully opposed reducing Gaozong's titles, before long he was sent out to govern Ruizhou. Right Remonstrance Officer Lü Zhi memorialized: "If today the court transfers a remonstrance officer because of a dispute with a chief minister, and tomorrow dismisses a remonstrance officer, then when chief ministers err hereafter, who will dare speak?"
降封高宗事 is a dispute over reducing Gaozong’s titles/fief; ‘demoting and enfeoffing’ splits 降封 into two contrary acts.

Bureau director Zhang Jun was then inspecting troops at Jinling. Chou Yu urged a plan on him: "The Jin have massed their army in Huaidong; their troops are weary and their supplies exhausted. Send twenty thousand elite troops—one column from Shouyang, one from the Han River—straight for the old capital, and the enemy should withdraw without a fight. Then follow with a larger army, and success is certain.

Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun was then inspecting troops at Jinling. Chou Yu urged a plan on him: "The Jin have massed their army in Huaidong; their troops are weary and their supplies exhausted. Send twenty thousand elite troops—one column from Shouyang, one from the Han River—straight for the old capital, and the enemy should withdraw without a fight. Then follow with a larger army, and success is certain.
樞密使 is the Military Affairs Commissioner, not a generic bureau director.

Bureau Director Zhang Jun was then inspecting troops at Jinling; Yu urged him with a plan: "The Jin have heavy forces in Huaidong; their army is weary and provisions exhausted. If twenty thousand elite troops—one column from Shouyang, one from the Han River—strike straight for the old capital, the enemy should withdraw without battle; then a great army can follow in pursuit, and nothing will fail.

Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun was then inspecting troops at Jinling; Yu urged him with a plan: "The Jin have heavy forces in Huaidong; their army is weary and provisions exhausted. If twenty thousand elite troops—one column from Shouyang, one from the Han River—strike straight for the old capital, the enemy should withdraw without battle; then a great army can follow in pursuit, and nothing will fail.
樞密使 is the Military Affairs Commissioner; Bureau Director misranks the office.

At that time the cave tribes and Liao were not yet pacified; he was advanced to Direct Academician and made Hunan Pacification Commissioner, forbade illicit coiners, urged people to farm, prices were stabilized, and merchants then traveled freely.

At that time the cave tribes were not yet pacified; he was advanced to Direct Academician and made Hunan Pacification Commissioner, forbade illicit coiners, urged people to farm, prices were stabilized, and merchants then traveled freely.
峒獠 is one designation for southwestern hill peoples; 獠 is not the Khitan Liao, so ‘and Liao’ invents a second group.

He planned to return south. Suddenly he heard that Bangchang had been sent to distant prefectures and that petty men were being dismissed one after another—seventeen or eighteen matching what he had urged—and Deng rejoiced, "Now I may speak fully."

He planned to return south. Suddenly he heard that Bangchang had been sent to distant prefectures and that petty men were being dismissed one after another—seven or eight in ten matching what he had urged—and Deng rejoiced, "Now I may speak fully."
十七八 is the approximate fraction seven or eight tenths, not the cardinals seventeen or eighteen.

He therefore planned to return south; suddenly he heard that Bangchang had each been given distant prefectures and that petty men of the moment were dismissed one after another—seventeen or eight out of ten matching what he had said—and Deng rejoiced: "Now one may speak fully."

He therefore planned to return south; suddenly he heard that Bangchang had been given a distant prefecture and that petty men of the moment were dismissed one after another—seven or eight out of ten matching what he had said—and Deng rejoiced: "Now one may speak fully."
十七八 is seven or eight tenths, not ‘seventeen or eight out of ten’; ‘had each’ also misattaches 各 to singular 邦昌.
Deng declined but could not refuse. With nowhere else to put the money, he placed it with the school and bought books to thank the people.
Deng declined but could not refuse. With nowhere else to put the money, he asked that it be placed with the school and used to buy books to thank the scholars and people.
請置於學 is a request to lodge the gift with the school, and 士民 is scholars and people; the original omits both.
Cultured sons and cultured grandsons, fit to be rulers and kings, suffered calamities, cut off like a belt's end.
Cultured sons and cultured grandsons, fit to be rulers and kings, met with calamities, yet were not cut off, continuing like a sash.
不斷如帶 means the line continued unbroken like a sash; the original reverses 不 and treats the image as severance.

Your servant is truly reckless; last year he submitted a memorial requesting Your Majesty to take a worthy Taizu grandson, treat his rank as imperial prince, and let him govern the nine provinces; he mistakenly received adoption and hearing and was pardoned rather than executed.

Your servant is truly reckless; last year he submitted a memorial requesting Your Majesty to take a worthy Taizu grandson, treat his rank as imperial prince, and let him govern the nine provinces; he mistakenly received the throne's heed and was pardoned rather than executed.
采聽 is the throne’s taking up and heeding the memorial, not familial or legal adoption; ‘a hearing of his proposal’ keeps 聽 but drops 采.

Chief councilor Qin Hui, whom Fu Zhirou had recommended, hated him and prompted critics to charge Yinliang with concealing his father's death. The Court of Judicial Review found no truth in it, yet he was still dismissed for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.

Chief councilor Qin Hui, because Fu Zhirou had recommended him, hated him and prompted critics to charge Yinliang with concealing his father's death. The Court of Judicial Review found no truth in it, yet he was still dismissed for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.
以其直柔所薦 is causal: Qin Hui hated Yinliang because Zhirou had recommended him; the original relative clause makes Zhirou Qin Hui’s recommender.

Chief Councilor Qin Hui, whom Zhirou had recommended for his bluntness, hated him; he prompted critics to impeach Yinliang for concealing his father's death without reporting mourning; the case went to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation and was unfounded, yet he was still punished for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register, dismissed, and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.

Chief Councilor Qin Hui, because Zhirou had recommended him, hated him; he prompted critics to impeach Yinliang for concealing his father's death without reporting mourning; the case went to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation and was unfounded, yet he was still punished for a clansman's falsely occupying an official household register, dismissed, and sent to the Ministry of Personnel—thereby ruined.
直柔 is the personal name Zhirou, not ‘bluntness’; 以…所薦 marks why Qin Hui hated Yinliang.
